Q1. Which of the following statements is correct?
A. We can assume a “perfect sphere” model when analyzing the bending motion
of a gymnast’s wrist.
This is incorrect because detailed limb motion depends on shape and joint geometry, so a
spherical approximation is not appropriate.
B. We can reasonably treat a parade float as a point mass when estimating how
far it travels over several kilometers in a given time.
Over kilometer-scale motion, the object’s size is negligible compared with its displacement, so
a point-mass model is appropriate.
C. We are never allowed to model motion as if it occurred in a vacuum when we
want to neglect air resistance.
This is incorrect because “vacuum” is a standard idealization used precisely to ignore drag
effects when they are small.
D. None of the above is correct.
This is incorrect because option B describes a valid and commonly used approximation.

Q7. A water droplet is launched from a fountain nozzle with speed v0 at an
angle θ above the horizontal. What is the speed of the droplet when it reaches
its maximum height (ignore air resistance)?
A. v0.
This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero, so the total speed is less
than v0 (unless θ = 0).
B. v0 cos θ.
This is correct because at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero and the horizontal
component remains v0 cos θ.
C. v0 sin θ.
This is incorrect because v0 sin θ is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at the
top.
D. 0.
This is incorrect because the droplet still has horizontal velocity at the top unless launched
straight up.

Q9. If the magnitudes of both charges are quadrupled and their separation is
doubled, what happens to the magnitude of the electrostatic force that each
charge exerts on the other?
A. It stays the same.
This is incorrect because changing charges and distance changes F ∝ q1q2/r2 unless the factors
exactly cancel.
B. It decreases by a factor of 4.
This is incorrect because the charges increase the force rather than decrease it.
C. It increases by a factor of 2.
This is incorrect because the combined scaling gives a larger factor than 2.
D. It increases by a factor of 4.
This is correct because F ∝ (4q)(4q)/(2r)
2 = 16/4 = 4 times the original force.
E. It increases by a factor of 16.
This is incorrect because it accounts for the charge increase (×16) but ignores the distance￾squared decrease (÷4).

Q12. A 3.0 kg rubber ball initially moving at 4.0 m/s strikes a wall and rebounds
at a speed of 2.5 m/s in the opposite direction. The collision lasts for 0.15 s.
What is the average force exerted on the ball during the collision (magnitude)?
A. 130 N
This is correct because Favg = |∆p|/∆t = m|vf − vi
|/∆t = 3.0 × |(−2.5) − 4.0|/0.15 = 130 N.
B. 30 N
This is incorrect because it underestimates the impulse by not accounting for the velocity
reversal.
C. 80 N
This is incorrect because it typically results from using the wrong collision time or the wrong
change in velocity.
D. None of the above is correct.
This is incorrect because the impulse calculation gives a magnitude of 130 N, which is listed.
